claims.text: The platform's own recorded distances establish a deviation of 1.40 km on this trip: trip_record.optimal_distance_km is 8.1 km and trip_record.actual_distance_km is 9.5 km, and POL-RD-22 measures the deviation as the difference between exactly those two recorded figures (9.5 - 8.1 = 1.40 km). POL-RD-22 sets the tolerance at 1.0 km, so this deviation is over tolerance and the within-tolerance rows of the refund matrix are shut out.

The GPS trace confirms which route was actually taken and when, as POL-RD-22 says the trace is used for: fixes run along Clementi Avenue 6 and Commonwealth Avenue West between 08:42:52 and 08:53:22 - roads that do not appear in the recommended route via (PIE, Clementi Road, Holland Road) - immediately after the platform logged the route deviation at the PIE / Clementi Avenue 6 exit at 08:42:55 and immediately before the logged rejoin at Holland Road / Commonwealth Avenue West at 08:53:16. The reroute is real, continuous for roughly ten minutes, and not a measurement artefact.

The driver did not inform the rider of the deviation, as POL-RD-21 requires him to do before or at the point of deviation (08:42:55). The chat log carries only two messages, sent at 08:35:52 and 08:36:12 - both before the trip even started at 08:37:22, and both about the driver's position at the pickup ('I'm at Westgate taxi stand') and the rider's acknowledgement ('Ok'). The trip record's messages-during-trip list is empty and in_app_calls is empty, so no recorded call can carry the verbal notice POL-RD-21 contemplates, and the rider never agreed to any deviation. The driver's own filing concedes the point: 'Forgot to inform, sorry.'

On POL-RD-24's matrix, exactly one row applies and only two are open on this record: (b) traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km, and (d) not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km. Both rows pay the rider the excess distance fare, so the rider's refund does not depend on how the traffic question is resolved. Row (a) - the only no-refund row for an over-tolerance deviation - is unavailable, because it also requires that the rider was informed and agreed, and on this record he was neither informed nor asked.

The LTA advisory in the record does not move this case into row (a) even taken at its highest: the artifact itself returns null for whether it intersects the recommended route and null for whether it justifies the reroute, and its own note says the record does not say whether the advisory lies on the recommended route, so POL-RD-23's requirement that the advisory intersect the recommended route is undetermined rather than made out. More importantly it is not decisive either way - if the reroute is held traffic-justified, the case is row (b) and the excess distance fare is refunded; if it is not, the case is row (d) and the excess distance fare is refunded in full.

The quantum follows from POL-RD-24's formula: the excess distance fare is the deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge, rounded to the cent - 1.40 km x 0.72 SGD = 1.01 SGD, which is the figure the fare ledger's own derived money block carries. The fare was metered and charged on 9.5 km (distance_fare 6.84 SGD within a total_charged of 14.78 SGD), so the extra 1.40 km is exactly what the rider paid for and did not need.

The rider still carries the disputed charge, which is what the outcome must cure: the fare ledger shows payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00 and no cancellation fee, so nothing has been returned to him yet. POL-GEN-03 defines PARTIAL_REFUND as part of the trip's charge being returned, and that is the rider win available here - the rider is owed the excess distance fare of 1.01 SGD. I do not press for more than the policy provides: the 4.00 SGD the rider asked for is his own estimate, and POL-RD-24 measures the refund by the excess distance fare alone, so 1.01 SGD, not 4.00 SGD, is the correct measure of what he is owed on this record.

claims.text: The driver's reroute was traffic-justified, so this case falls in row (b) of POL-RD-24 rather than row (d), and the driver's conduct is the conduct POL-RD-23 permits. The LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-05004-01 reports HEAVY_TRAFFIC on the Pan-Island Expressway towards Changi between the Clementi Avenue 6 exit and the Clementi Road exit; the recommended route on this trip (EV-TRIP-05004) runs along the PIE to Clementi Road in that direction, so on road, direction and location the advisory intersects the recommended route; and its window 08:15:42-09:27:22 overlaps the trip 08:37:22-08:55:22. The driver's account that the PIE was jammed after Clementi is therefore corroborated by traffic data rather than standing on his assertion alone.

The driver does not dispute that he failed to inform the rider of the deviation before or at the point of deviation, so row (a) of POL-RD-24 (informed and agreed, no refund) is not available and the most that can be ordered is the excess distance fare. The chat log EV-CHAT-05004 contains only two messages, both sent before the trip began and neither concerning a reroute, and the trip record EV-TRIP-05004 shows no in-app calls and no messages during the trip (messages_during_trip is empty). The notification obligation in POL-RD-21 is therefore breached and the case is confined to row (b).

The refund is capped at the excess distance fare of 1.01 SGD, not the 4.00 SGD the rider asks for. The deviation is 1.40 km (actual 9.5 km less recommended 8.1 km, EV-TRIP-05004) and the metered rate is 0.72 SGD per km (EV-FARE-05004); 1.40 x 0.72 = 1.01 SGD without surge, which is the exact figure POL-RD-24 fixes for rows (b) and (d). The rider's asserted figure of 4.00 has no support in the matrix, and the balance of the claim must be refused.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the rider is owed the excess distance fare of 1.01 SGD, and nothing more. Why.

1) The deviation is established. POL-RD-22 measures it as the platform's recorded actual distance minus the recorded recommended distance: 9.5 km − 8.1 km = 1.40 km (EV-TRIP-05004). POL-RD-22's tolerance is 1.0 km, so 1.40 km is over tolerance and the within-tolerance no-refund rows are shut out. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-05004) is used only to show which route was taken: its fixes run along Clementi Avenue 6 and Commonwealth Avenue West between 08:42:52 and 08:53:22, immediately after the platform logged the departure from the recommended route at the PIE / Clementi Avenue 6 exit (08:42:55) and immediately before the logged rejoin at Holland Road / Commonwealth Avenue West (08:53:16). The reroute is real.

2) The driver did not inform the rider. POL-RD-21 requires notice by in-app chat, or verbally with the trip call recording as evidence, before or at the point of deviation (08:42:55). EV-CHAT-05004 carries only two messages, both before the trip started and both about the pickup point; EV-TRIP-05004 records messages_during_trip as empty and in_app_calls as empty. No recorded call can carry a verbal notice. The driver's own statement concedes it: 'Forgot to inform, sorry.' Row (a) of the refund matrix, the only no-refund row for an over-tolerance deviation, is therefore unavailable.

3) The traffic question does not change the money. The LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-05004-01 reports HEAVY_TRAFFIC on the PIE towards Changi between the Clementi Avenue 6 exit and the Clementi Road exit, with a window (08:15:42–09:27:22) that overlaps the trip (08:37:22–08:55:22). Road, direction of travel and location all sit on the recommended route segment, so POL-RD-23's requirement that the advisory intersect the recommended route and overlap the window is satisfied on this record and the reroute is traffic-justified — row (b). Even if it were not, the case would fall in row (d). Both rows pay the same thing: the excess distance fare (POL-RD-24).

4) The quantum. POL-RD-24 fixes the excess distance fare as deviation distance × fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge, rounded to the cent: 1.40 km × 0.72 SGD = 1.01 SGD, which is the figure EV-FARE-05004's own money block carries. The rider's asserted 4.00 SGD is his own estimate and is not the measure POL-RD-24 provides; the balance of that claim is refused. Nothing has been returned yet (EV-FARE-05004: payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), so the amount is still outstanding.

5) Outcome. The rider filed, and he is owed less than the 4.00 SGD he contested, so the ruling is PARTIAL_REFUND of the part owed: 1.01 SGD, with driver_compensation_sgd null. A route deviation has no referral clause in this version, so referrals is empty. Confidence 0.90: every artifact that carries the deciding facts (EV-TRIP-05004, EV-FARE-05004, EV-CHAT-05004) is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, the deviation and its measure are agreed on both sides, and the only incidental open point — whether the advisory precisely overlays the recommended segment — does not affect the amount either way.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties agree on the money, so the case is decided on the platform's own recorded distances under POL-RD-22 and the refund matrix in POL-RD-24.

What is established. The trip record (EV-TRIP-05004) records an optimal route of 8.1 km and an actual distance of 9.5 km. POL-RD-22 measures the deviation as exactly those two recorded figures, and the GPS trace is not used to re-measure distance: 9.5 - 8.1 = 1.40 km. That is above POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance, so the within-tolerance rows of the matrix (rows (c) and (e), no refund) are shut out. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-05004) confirms which route was taken: fixes run along Clementi Avenue 6 and Commonwealth Avenue West from 08:42:52 to 08:53:22, between the platform-logged deviation at the PIE / Clementi Avenue 6 exit (08:42:55) and the rejoin at Holland Road / Commonwealth Avenue West (08:53:16). The reroute is real.

Why no refund is refused. Row (a) — the only no-refund row for an over-tolerance deviation — requires that the rider was informed and agreed. He was not. The chat log (EV-CHAT-05004) holds only two messages, at 08:35:52 and 08:36:12, both before the trip began at 08:37:22 and both about the pickup point; the trip record's messages-during-trip list is empty and in_app_calls is empty, so no recorded call carries a verbal notice under POL-RD-21. The driver's own statement concedes it: 'Forgot to inform, sorry.' POL-RD-21's notification duty was therefore breached, and the driver's advocate does not contest it. Row (a) is unavailable.

Why the traffic question does not change the result. ledger.claim: The platform's own recorded distances establish a deviation of 1.40 km on this trip: trip_record.optimal_distance_km is 8.1 km and trip_record.actual_distance_km is 9.5 km, and POL-RD-22 measures the deviation as the difference between exactly those two recorded figures (9.5 - 8.1 = 1.40 km). POL-RD-22 sets the tolerance at 1.0 km, so this deviation is over tolerance and the within-tolerance rows of the refund matrix are shut out.

The GPS trace confirms which route was actually taken and when, as POL-RD-22 says the trace is used for: fixes run along Clementi Avenue 6 and Commonwealth Avenue West between 08:42:52 and 08:53:22 - roads that do not appear in the recommended route via (PIE, Clementi Road, Holland Road) - immediately after the platform logged the route deviation at the PIE / Clementi Avenue 6 exit at 08:42:55 and immediately before the logged rejoin at Holland Road / Commonwealth Avenue West at 08:53:16. The reroute is real, continuous for roughly ten minutes, and not a measurement artefact.

The driver did not inform the rider of the deviation, as POL-RD-21 requires him to do before or at the point of deviation (08:42:55). The chat log carries only two messages, sent at 08:35:52 and 08:36:12 - both before the trip even started at 08:37:22, and both about the driver's position at the pickup ('I'm at Westgate taxi stand') and the rider's acknowledgement ('Ok'). The trip record's messages-during-trip list is empty and in_app_calls is empty, so no recorded call can carry the verbal notice POL-RD-21 contemplates, and the rider never agreed to any deviation. The driver's own filing concedes the point: 'Forgot to inform, sorry.'

On POL-RD-24's matrix, exactly one row applies and only two are open on this record: (b) traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km, and (d) not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km. Both rows pay the rider the excess distance fare, so the rider's refund does not depend on how the traffic question is resolved. Row (a) - the only no-refund row for an over-tolerance deviation - is unavailable, because it also requires that the rider was informed and agreed, and on this record he was neither informed nor asked.

The LTA advisory in the record does not move this case into row (a) even taken at its highest: the artifact itself returns null for whether it intersects the recommended route and null for whether it justifies the reroute, and its own note says the record does not say whether the advisory lies on the recommended route, so POL-RD-23's requirement that the advisory intersect the recommended route is undetermined rather than made out. More importantly it is not decisive either way - if the reroute is held traffic-justified, the case is row (b) and the excess distance fare is refunded; if it is not, the case is row (d) and the excess distance fare is refunded in full.

The quantum follows from POL-RD-24's formula: the excess distance fare is the deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge, rounded to the cent - 1.40 km x 0.72 SGD = 1.01 SGD, which is the figure the fare ledger's own derived money block carries. The fare was metered and charged on 9.5 km (distance_fare 6.84 SGD within a total_charged of 14.78 SGD), so the extra 1.40 km is exactly what the rider paid for and did not need.

The rider still carries the disputed charge, which is what the outcome must cure: the fare ledger shows payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00 and no cancellation fee, so nothing has been returned to him yet. POL-GEN-03 defines PARTIAL_REFUND as part of the trip's charge being returned, and that is the rider win available here - the rider is owed the excess distance fare of 1.01 SGD. I do not press for more than the policy provides: the 4.00 SGD the rider asked for is his own estimate, and POL-RD-24 measures the refund by the excess distance fare alone, so 1.01 SGD, not 4.00 SGD, is the correct measure of what he is owed on this record.

The driver's reroute was traffic-justified, so this case falls in row (b) of POL-RD-24 rather than row (d), and the driver's conduct is the conduct POL-RD-23 permits. The LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-05004-01 reports HEAVY_TRAFFIC on the Pan-Island Expressway towards Changi between the Clementi Avenue 6 exit and the Clementi Road exit; the recommended route on this trip (EV-TRIP-05004) runs along the PIE to Clementi Road in that direction, so on road, direction and location the advisory intersects the recommended route; and its window 08:15:42-09:27:22 overlaps the trip 08:37:22-08:55:22. The driver's account that the PIE was jammed after Clementi is therefore corroborated by traffic data rather than standing on his assertion alone.

The driver does not dispute that he failed to inform the rider of the deviation before or at the point of deviation, so row (a) of POL-RD-24 (informed and agreed, no refund) is not available and the most that can be ordered is the excess distance fare. The chat log EV-CHAT-05004 contains only two messages, both sent before the trip began and neither concerning a reroute, and the trip record EV-TRIP-05004 shows no in-app calls and no messages during the trip (messages_during_trip is empty). The notification obligation in POL-RD-21 is therefore breached and the case is confined to row (b).

The refund is capped at the excess distance fare of 1.01 SGD, not the 4.00 SGD the rider asks for. The deviation is 1.40 km (actual 9.5 km less recommended 8.1 km, EV-TRIP-05004) and the metered rate is 0.72 SGD per km (EV-FARE-05004); 1.40 x 0.72 = 1.01 SGD without surge, which is the exact figure POL-RD-24 fixes for rows (b) and (d). The rider's asserted figure of 4.00 has no support in the matrix, and the balance of the claim must be refused.
